reason: Per-site verified (RFC 0106 wave 4b): the inner `map` of connection_handler.rb:75-79 is the same Ruby-Enumerable idiom, spelled as the body of trails' explicit `for..of` accumulation.

connection_handler.rb:118 `resolve_pool_config(config, owner_name, role, shard)` — Rails resolves the adapter class from `db_config.adapter` by requiring it at connect time. ESM has no autoload-by-name, so the factory is threaded as an `adapterFactory` kwarg; this is the same cause already reviewed on this file's `resolve_pool_config -> new` row.
connection_handler.rb:78 `Concurrent::Map.new(initial_capacity: 2)` — a JS `Map` has no capacity hint, so the kwarg has no counterpart to pass. Language shortcoming, not deferred work.

RFC 0099 bucket (c) tooling noise, verified at connection_adapters/abstract/connection_handler.rb:279 `ConnectionAdapters::PoolConfig.new(connection_name, db_config, role, shard)`: the two bodies each construct more than one object (or the port raises a guard Rails does not), and the comparator pairs the `new` occurrences positionally, so this row compares two unrelated constructions rather than a matched call site.
